decisions.coordinateRole: public campground/riverside access-area anchor; exact paddling launch and water-entry coordinate not published
decisions.reason: Recreation.gov places the public campground on the South Fork Ogden and describes river access, tubing, fishing, paved roads and parking. It does not identify a dedicated kayak/canoe launch or wet-edge coordinate. Retain the useful riverside site as an area anchor and state that limitation rather than calling it a water-entry point.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the optional intermediate access-area marker with corrected name and note; no coordinate change.

decisions.site: Little North Fork Reservoir backwaters take-out
decisions.coordinateRole: candidate endpoint coordinate near Dworshak Reservoir backwaters; public land access, vehicle staging and exact take-out not verified
decisions.reason: American Whitewater and North Idaho Rivers describe a remote take-out bridge and a severe, poorly marked shuttle; Riverfacts supplies the candidate backwaters point. Idaho Fish and Game lists no boat ramp or dock for the Little North Fork water record. No current managing-agency source verifies lawful access, vehicle staging or boat pickup at this coordinate. Keep the endpoint record for follow-up and withhold the route.
decisions.reopeningCondition: A current land manager confirms lawful public take-out access, vehicle staging or boat pickup, and a coordinate for the intended endpoint.

decisions.site: Fort Mill River Access below Lake Wylie Dam (water-entry edge)
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Fort Mill public landing below Lake Wylie Dam
decisions.coordinateRole: SCDNR Fort Mill Access Pier public-access feature OBJECTID 739; access-area geometry, not survey-grade wet-edge precision
decisions.reason: SCDNR's current public water-access feature OBJECTID 739 names Fort Mill Access Pier on the Catawba River, with Active status, Open public access, Duke Energy ownership/maintenance and 15 parking spaces. Its geometry provides a defensible replacement approximately 428 feet from the old stored point. SCDNR's scenic-river page independently describes the public Fort Mill landing, ramp and parking just downstream of Lake Wylie Dam. A similarly named SCDNR boat ramp feature is on Lake Wylie above the dam, so it was not substituted.
decisions.publicationAction: Source coordinates and labels are corrected. Hold all three dependent routes until fresh canonical geometry is generated and inspected; @paddletoday/geo is missing, so current generated route assets still have the old endpoint.

decisions.coordinateRole: public park scout/portage and difficult carry-in access-area anchor; not an easy default launch
decisions.reason: Manitowoc County identifies a riverfront park with stair access to the river. The Manitowoc River Watershed water-trail plan lists Lower Cato Falls as a difficult carry-in access site with steep slopes. Retain the location for the documented scout/portage and carry context, and clarify the difficult access; no exact wet-edge coordinate is published.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the site anchor with an explicit difficult-carry and scouting caveat; no coordinate change.

decisions.coordinateRole: official dock address/access-area anchor; exact wet-edge coordinate not published
decisions.reason: TECHE Project lists the official Charenton dock at 3726 Chitimacha Trail at mile 91.0. The source confirms site identity and public paddle-trail status by address, but not a surveyed water-entry coordinate. Keep the current access-area point, correct its label, and stop presenting its precision as the dock edge.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the five routes and retain the coordinate as an address/access-area anchor; no coordinate change.

decisions.site: Edward H. McCabe Preserve public floating canoe dock
decisions.coordinateRole: approximate river-side anchor; not a published dock coordinate
decisions.reason: The Nature Conservancy confirms a public non-motorized floating dock at the end of the roughly two-mile Milton canoe trail and says to find the dock on the river's south side. Its published GPS is for overland trail parking, about a half-mile from the dock; no dock coordinate was found. The stored point is explicitly approximate and cannot support a precise take-out pin, so withhold the route while retaining the record.
decisions.reopeningCondition: TNC or a defensible manager map/GIS source establishes the dock's location sufficiently to replace the approximate point.

decisions.site: Valley Falls State Park river-right put-in / superintendent office
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Valley Falls State Park river-right check-in / access area
decisions.coordinateRole: required river-right park check-in/access area; not a surveyed water-entry point
decisions.reason: American Whitewater documents river-right sign-in with Valley Falls State Park personnel as a required step before this expert run. The stored point is intentionally named at the park office/check-in area, which paddlers must visit; the exact river-entry pixel is not published. Rename the marker so it no longer claims that the office coordinate is the wet edge and preserve the sign-in requirement.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the required check-in/access-area anchor and park permission requirement; no coordinate change.

decisions.site: Holiday Heights Park / Holiday Heights Landing
decisions.coordinateRole: public canoe landing/park access-area anchor; not a surveyed water-entry point
decisions.reason: Onalaska's redevelopment plan identifies an accessible canoe launch at public Holiday Heights Park. The city facility listing confirms the public park, and Wisconsin River Trips describes the specific public take-out with parking. The exact wet-edge coordinate is not published, so retain the current area anchor and link the manager evidence.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the take-out and retain the current coordinate as an access-area anchor; no coordinate change.

decisions.coordinateRole: Jane Addams Trailhead / boat-launch access-area anchor; exact wet-edge point not published
decisions.reason: The Freeport Park District-managed Jane Addams Trail site lists Wes Block Trail Access at 2636 W Fairview Road with parking, shelter, restroom and a boat launch. It does not publish a launch-edge coordinate. Retain the trailhead coordinate as an access-area anchor and clarify its role; do not snap it to the river centerline.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the route and label the coordinate as a trailhead/access-area anchor; no coordinate change.

decisions.coordinateRole: NPS Gilbert horse-trailhead coordinate; not verified as the river take-out
decisions.reason: NPS confirms Gilbert as a river access and the route's endpoint, but the stored coordinate exactly matches the NPS Getting Around table's Gilbert Horse trailhead entry. NPS separately publishes a different coordinate for Gilbert Primitive camping and warns that GPS is unreliable; neither source provides the exact gravel-bar take-out point. Retain the route record but withhold it until the actual public water-access coordinate is established.
decisions.reopeningCondition: An NPS map or current access record identifies the actual Gilbert gravel-bar boat take-out coordinate and approach.
